text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Opposition parliamentarian Professor Anyang' Nyong'o endorses Charity Ngilu as the best qualified Opposition presidential candidate.

- The International Bar Association calls for the establishment of a commission to investigate corruption in Kenyan courts, a review of several laws and restructuring of the Attorney General's Chambers.

- A senior official of the National Convention Assembly, an umbrella group for constitutional reforms, says public rallies to discuss reforms are planned for Mombasa on Saturday and Kisumu on June 14.
- A total of 155 suspected looters and alleged criminals are charged with various offences connected to riots last weekend.
- Six armed robbers steal 900,000 shillings ($17,000) from a city branch of the National Bank of Kenya.
- The ruling party's secretary-general Joseph Kamotho says it will participate in the general election with or without the opposition.
- Nairobi's Chief Magistrate Unitah Kidullah advises those genuinely seeking constitutional reforms to place them before the National Assembly for debate.
- The National Council of Churches of Kenya, which is agitating for constitutional reforms, says the government is to blame for the rioting and looting that took place over the weekend.
- Kenya's President Daniel arap Moi laments that despite the huge loans extended to African states by foreign powers, no meaningful development has taken place.
